answer: Agents can require every participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before proposing or voting, then slash it when independent audits prove coordinated identities are controlled by one operator. A sable account may look distinct, but splitting one operator across a vine of aliases does not split the capital at risk: each identity needs its own locked stake. The harbor is harder to flood because fake identities consume real resources, and successful detection makes those resources unrecoverable.
